correctness.rationale: For homogeneous independent survival, the variance is a²q(1-q)+b²q^m(1-q^m). On q in (1/2,2^(-1/m)) derivative roots are equivalent to t=h_m(q), and h_m derivative has the sign of explicit H_m. Seven exact rational Bernstein certificates establish H_m>0 for m=2..6 (for m=6 on three subintervals). For m>=7, signs of H_m at 1/2,7/10,2^(-1/m) are +,-,+ and Descartes caps positive roots at two, giving the sharp threshold. For eight tips with pendant lengths 1 and 4/5 plus seven leaves of 1/10000, the exact variance derivative signs at q=1/2,3/5,7/10,9/10 are +,-,+,-; the derivative has exactly three positive roots by sign variation, so exactly two maxima. Independently reconstructed the rational derivative and all four signs. Source script independently enumerates the complete 256-survivor polynomial and re-derives Bernstein coefficients; it is corroboration of the analytic proof.
residual_risks: The seven-clade minimum holds only for the defined reduced two-block model, not for arbitrary rooted trees.
m>=7 proof uses an all-integers rational/geometric inequality, not 94-instance verification alone.

value.rationale: A complete sharp clade-size cutoff in a natural two-event survival model, with explicit proof of unimodality below threshold, and a strictly positive small tree showing the phenomenon is not a zero-edge artifact. This is a motivated mathematical phase boundary, not merely a new sample of known bimodality.
